title: AdminUserRow
description: One row of the operator console's user table, derived from identity_application::administration::AdminUserRow. This is a DIFFERENT type from the self-service AccountView for the same account, and the difference is the point: an administrative read is not a self-service read, and the two are separate so that a field cannot be added to one and appear in the other by accident.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; SearchUsersQuery has no body and no route serves it

user_id.description: The user. A transparent UUID newtype in Rust.

role.description: The platform role. Decides what an administrator may do to an ACCOUNT — never consulted about a merge in another repository (ADR-0005). may_assign_roles() is true for support and administrator and false for member and service: support moderates, it does not promote.

status.description: The account's status. Only active permits authentication (UserStatus::permits_authentication), and the status is the authoritative gate — a stale session must still be refused. pending_verification means the user can complete a challenge but has no session.

active_sessions.description: How many live sessions the user holds. A COUNT, not a list: an administrative view of session state is a number for a table, and the session identifiers are the self-service surface's business.

last_authenticated_at_ms.description: When they last signed in, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Null means never. Serialised as null, not omitted.
last_authenticated_at_ms.x-serde-note: Option<i64> with no skip_serializing_if, so the key is always present.

created_at_ms.description: When the account was created, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

x-on-suspension: Suspension is a POST and not a field write on purpose: it is a command with an effect the server records in the audit trail, and modelling it as an edit-status control would invite a console that offers a generic field. It also revokes the user's sessions server-side, so the effect is NOT complete when the call returns a user row — a console must report what the server said, not what it assumed.
